newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end down but off lows.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end down but off lows.

text.p: China's B share indices fell on corrections on Friday but ended off their lows helped by an afternoon rebound in the domestic A share markets, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index fell 0.71 percent to 70.439 points after hitting a low of 69.122 points. Turnover was $12 million against Thursday's $18.1 million.
Shenzhen's B index lost 0.27 percent to 165.08 points. Turnover was HK$150.3 million, down from HK$269.6 million on Thursday.

Widespread rumours saying the Shanghai exchange would cancel the three-day and seven-day state debt repurchase contracts starting from next Monday were one of the factors depressing shares on the bourse on Friday, brokers said.
The Shanghai Stock Exchange denied it was considering cancelling the contracts, which are a major source of liquidity for China's stock markets.

"Investors are concerned that the authorities are drafting measures to counter over-speculation, and there is talk that it might abolish some repo contracts," a trader with Central-South Securities said.
On Shanghai's B share market, retailer Shanghai Friendship & Overseas Chinese Co was the biggest loser on liquidation, falling $0.022 or 4.91 percent to $0.426 on volume of 517,300 shares.
Shanghai Diesel Engine Co traded the most on institutional liquidation on expectations of unpromising 1996 results, falling $0.016 or 3.21 percent to $0.482 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
On the Shenzhen B share market, diesel engine producer Changchai Co was the biggest loser, dropping HK$0.26 or 3.27 percent to HK$7.68 on volume of 1.86 million shares.
The A share markets in both Shanghai and Shenzhen reversed their morning losses to close higher, brokers said.
Shanghai's A share index was up 0.8 percent to 1,177.849 points after hitting an intraday low of 1,142.812 points. Turnover was 8.3 billion yuan, down from 8.8 billion yuan on Thursday.
Wuhan Twin-Tigers Coatings was the star on talk of a plan to offer bonus shares, soaring 0.93 yuan to its 10 percent limit-up of 10.18 yuan on volume of 3.9 million shares.
Shenzhen's A index ended up 1.27 percent at 416.17 points, rebounding from an intraday low of 405.94, on turnover of 8.4 billion yuan, compared with Thursday's 8.94 billion.
Building materials producer Shenzhen Universe was the best performer, gaining 0.98 yuan or 10 percent limit-up to 10.73 yuan after 11.2 million shares changed hands.
